name: Cross-body stretch
movement: one arm drawn across the chest with the other hand and held

phone.placement: Stand the phone up on the floor, two or three metres away, facing you.

words.hint: Facing the phone, one arm drawn across the chest with the other hand, held.
words.start: Stand the phone up on the floor. Stand facing it, draw one arm across your chest with the other hand, and hold.
words.position: Stand facing the phone. Bring the stiff arm across your chest and use the other hand above the elbow to draw it gently further, until a stretch is felt at the back of the shoulder.
words.top: The arm drawn across the chest, elbow toward the other shoulder, held by the other hand on the upper arm; shoulders level and the chest facing the phone.
howto: Stand facing the phone. Lift the stiff arm to about chest height and bring it across your body.
With the other hand on the upper arm, just above the elbow, draw it gently further across until you feel the stretch at the back of the shoulder.
Hold for the count. Shoulders level — don’t let the stretching shoulder hike up — and the chest facing the phone.
words.cannot: How strong the stretch feels, and where your hand holds — keep it on the upper arm, not the forearm or the elbow joint. It sees how far across the elbow is, the shoulders level and the chest facing the phone; a turn of the whole body is not seen.
words.about: Cross-body stretch — facing the phone: how far across, as the elbow's distance from its own shoulder toward the other, at least 40% of the shoulder width (about 30° across the chest); the stretching shoulder within 10° of where it started, since it hikes up under the pull; and the chest facing the phone, the shoulder width at least 85% of its width at the start. The clock runs while all three are right. Twenty seconds a hold, three holds.
words.lost: Stand facing the camera, both arms in the picture
words.hold: That is it — hold the stretch
words.safety: A pull at the back of the shoulder, not a pinch at the front. Ease off if it pinches.
words.harder: A longer hold; a little more draw across.
words.mistakes: Turning the body instead of drawing the arm across; hiking the shoulder; pulling on the forearm or pressing on the elbow joint — hold the upper arm.

measurements.label: hand from the far shoulder, % of trunk
measurements.why: The hand to the far shoulder, as a share of the trunk: not judged, it picks the working arm (the one drawn across).

measurements.label: elbow across

settings.label: Elbow across the body, at least (% of shoulder width)

measurements.why: How far the elbow has come across from its own shoulder toward the other, as a share of the shoulder width: about 30 with the arm 20° across, 45 at 30°, 60 at 40°. It reads the stretch whether the elbow is bent or straight.

measurements.label: how far across
measurements.why: The reach the other way up, so the arm across the chest is the larger of the two sides and is the one measured.

measurements.label: shoulder above the other
measurements.why: The shoulder line off level: the stretching shoulder hikes up under the pull.

measurements.label: shoulder width, % of start
measurements.why: The shoulder width against the hips, as a percent of its width at the start: turning toward the arm narrows it.

settings.label: Shoulder width, % of the start, at least

faults.label: Draw further
faults.text: Draw the arm further across your chest
faults.deep: Further across — draw the elbow toward the other shoulder

faults.label: Shoulder hiking
faults.text: Shoulder down — level with the other

faults.label: Side-bending
faults.text: Stay upright — don’t lean to the side

faults.label: Body turning
faults.text: Keep the chest facing the phone — draw the arm across, don’t turn
